text:
Marathon Petroleum rebounded 3.4% today after a rough two-week slide, likely catching a relief bounce as oil prices stabilized and refinery conditions remained solid. US crude held around $99.60 per barrel while refineries ran at 94.5% capacity—a healthy operating level—and gasoline inventories stayed moderate at just under 209 million barrels, suggesting steady demand is supporting the sector.

The stock's recovery also comes after several days of geopolitical whiplash: oil had briefly crashed on hopes of Iran peace talks, but those talks now look stalled (Secretary of State Rubio cited "little hope" of a breakthrough), and Trump administration officials remain targets of Iranian threats. That shift away from imminent de-escalation likely stopped the oil sell-off that had hammered refiners earlier this week, allowing Marathon to claw back ground.
